title: Talk to support or a consultant with Office 365 for business
description: Need to speak to someone right away? Admins, have your account details ready when you call Support. Learn more at the Office 365 Training Center: http://office.com/training

asr.full_text: If you need to talk to someone about Office 365 for your business, you can contact support. Or work with a consultant. Let's take a look at both. Sign into Office.com with your work email. And choose Admin. In the lower right corner, choose Need Help. Describe the problem, like adding a domain name from another provider, and you see a. Suggested support article, but it's one you've already read. Choose No, then Let us call you. Type or verify your phone number, then Call me. You'll receive a call in a few minutes from a support representative who will assist you. With Office 365. If you need help with a much bigger project. And prefer to work with an Office 365 consultant,. Visit microsoft.com slash solution dash providers. Enter a product like SharePoint and search in partners. Add your organization size and country. Then go. Select up to three providers. Then contact selected providers. Provide more details about your project. Then enter your contact information. And send. Then OK. You'll get a response within 72 hours,. And you can discuss your Office 365 needs. With a Microsoft Solution Provider.

textual.context: Presented as instructional Office 365 support guidance; the title and description also frame it as talking to support or a consultant. Promotion versus neutral training is unclear from the supplied records, but the wording describes a standard support workflow.
textual.potential_relevance: Support identity is linked to a requested sign-in and phone-number submission, followed by a promised support callback.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish who operates the page, whether the callback occurs, what information is collected beyond the stated phone number/work email sign-in, or whether any destination is legitimate.

textual.context: Presented as a workflow for finding an Office 365 consultant or Microsoft Solution Provider; no explicit warning or denial is present.
textual.potential_relevance: Microsoft Solution Provider identity is linked to selecting providers, submitting project and contact information, and a stated response timeframe.
textual.limitations: The records do not verify the destination, provider identities, response outcome, or any terms of service, fees, or follow-up requests.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents instructional guidance for business users and administrators seeking Office 365 support or consulting, including an ordinary support workflow requesting work-account and phone-number details. A separate consultant segment describes searching for solution providers, submitting project and contact details, and receiving a stated response within 72 hours, without describing a deceptive solicitation or unsupported outcome.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary content is an operational demonstration and tutorial for using Office 365 support tools and a solution-provider search workflow, including support navigation, provider selection, and contact submission.
